Prevention: Use weevil-free planting materials e.g. pared suckers and tissue culture plantlets.
Rake all trash from the area around banana plants to the interrow.
Make sure that the trash is pest and disease free otherwise it can be a source of further infection to new banana plants.
Chop all fallen and harvested pseudostems into small pieces so that they dry quickly.
When harvesting, cut the pseudostem at ground level, then cover the corm with soil.
Monitoring: Look for the presence of the weevil.
When they are newly emerged they are reddish-brown but soon become a dull black.
The weevils are nocturnal and hide during the day in and around corms and moist areas near the plant.
The larvae tunnel through the corms.
Check for adults in debris and around banana mats.
Other symptoms include snapping of the pseudostem, retarded and stunted growth, premature leaf drop and decreased bunch size and in severe cases the young suckers wither.
An average catch of 1 or more per trap per week requires control measures.
A trap is set by putting the flat side down of a split pseudostem.
Check under the pseudostem once per week.
Direct Control: Physically kill all weevils under 20-60cm pseudostem traps (100/ha).
Check the traps weekly and service them every 4 months.
Apply 60-100g of neem seed powder per hole at planting, then at 4 month intervals.
Restrictions: Use personal protective equipment when handling and applying pesticides, follow the label recommendations.
Do not eat, drink, smoke when mixing or applying pesticides.
Dissolve 2ml in 2-4 litres of water and spray with a knapsack sprayer in and around banana mats at the rate of 2-4 litres of spray solution per 100m2
No re-entry until the spray has dried.
Observe a 14- day preharvest period.Spray when the problem is noted
